title: Manipulating ratios
summary: Recap what a ratio is, then simplify ratios, write them as 1 : n and n : 1, and move between ratios and fractions: of the total, of a part, and a mixture, with three printable worksheets.

els.text: Simplify ratios, write them as 1 : n and n : 1, and move between ratios and fractions.

•  Explain what a ratio compares, and why the order matters
•  Simplify a ratio, and write it as 1 : n or n : 1
•  Write a ratio as a fraction of the total, or of another part
•  Write a ratio from a fraction

A cake needs $1$ egg for every $300$ g of flour. Ben has $400$ g of flour and says: "I need $100$ more flour, so I will add $100$ more eggs: $101$ eggs." What do you think of his plan? What should he do?
A ratio keeps quantities in proportion: $1$ egg to $300$ g of flour. Keep them in proportion and the recipe stays the same.
A ratio compares quantities, showing how much of one thing there is compared to another. Red : blue = $3 : 5$ means $3$ red for every $5$ blue.

els.text: What fraction of the beads are red?
Red : blue = $2 : 7$. Amara says $\frac{2}{7}$ of the beads are red. Kofi says $\frac{2}{9}$. Who is right? How would you convince the other?
It asks about all the beads, so the denominator is the total: add the parts.
Now: what fraction of the beads are blue?

slides.title: Of the total

items.title: red : blue = 3 : 5 What fraction of the beads are red?
question: red : blue = $3 : 5$
What fraction of the beads are red?
explanation:
Bar model: draw a row of boxes for each part of the ratio.
@bar {"parts":[],"rows":[{"name":"Red","units":3},{"name":"Blue","units":5}]}

Shade the red boxes (3). The total is every box: 8 parts.
@bar {"parts":[],"rows":[{"name":"Red","units":3,"role":"numerator"},{"name":"Blue","units":5}],"sideBrace":{"label":"total: 8 parts"}}
The denominator is the total: every part added.

els.text:
•  A ratio compares quantities in order, in step
•  Simplify by dividing every part by the same number; $1 : n$ and $n : 1$ make one part $1$
•  Of the total: add the parts. Of a part: that part is the denominator
•  Read the words after "of" to decide which
